_comment: Codex CLI hooks adapter: the git-push safety gate + secret-guard.mjs, both PreToolUse. Verification status, updated 2026-07-25 via a direct fetch of https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks (OpenAI's official Codex hooks reference, redirected from developers.openai.com/codex/hooks) -- schema-confirmed, still NOT tested against a live Codex CLI install (no configured model provider in this dev sandbox). What that fetch resolved, all previously open questions: (1) hooks are ENABLED BY DEFAULT (feature key `hooks`, `codex_hooks` a deprecated alias for the same flag; a third-party source claiming opt-in-required was checked directly against the primary docs and found wrong) -- no config.toml change needed to use this file. (2) `Bash` and `apply_patch` (file edits) both emit PreToolUse events, and BOTH scannable-content fields are the exact same JSON key -- `tool_input.command` -- confirmed directly, not guessed; secret-guard.mjs is now wired below using that confirmed field. (3) The stdin/stdout hook contract (`hookSpecificOutput.{hookEventName,permissionDecision,permissionDecisionReason}`) is byte-identical in shape to Claude Code's own -- Codex modeled its hooks system on it directly. Still genuinely open, disclosed rather than hidden: real GitHub issues (openai/codex#16732, #20204) report apply_patch hook events not firing consistently across all Codex CLI versions despite being documented as supported -- treat secret-guard.mjs as 'should fire per spec,' verify with a trivial known-bad edit on your own install before trusting it silently. Deliberately NOT included: the ExitPlanMode-matcher boardroom-checkpoint gate (Codex CLI has no plan-mode tool at all; it uses approval_policy instead -- nothing to gate here, not a missed port).

PreToolUse._matcher_comment: CONFIRMED via OpenAI's official Codex hooks docs: 'Bash' is a real, documented intercepted tool for PreToolUse/PostToolUse.

hooks._command_comment: Replace <PATH-TO-YOUR-INSTALLED-WINGMAN-PLUGIN> with wherever Claude Code's plugin marketplace installed Wingman on this machine (or a checked-out copy of the LabLaunchPad/Wingman repo). Reuses the real script unmodified -- see plugins/wingman/scripts/dod-pre-push-check.mjs, which already runs standalone with zero Claude Code involvement. Simpler and more robust than this hooks.json path: install it as a real git pre-push hook instead (item 3 of the harness-adapters README) -- that fires under any harness, including this one, with no Codex-specific wiring at all.
hooks.statusMessage: Wingman: checking Boardroom verdict, tests, and threat register before allowing a git push

hooks._command_comment: Ported from plugins/wingman/hooks/secret-guard.mjs -- blocks destructive commands and real secret patterns before they run. Real, tested (schema-verified via a synthetic stdin/stdout round-trip, not just written and assumed), not just written and assumed.
hooks.statusMessage: Wingman: scanning for destructive commands and secret patterns

PreToolUse._matcher_comment: CONFIRMED via the same official docs: file edits performed through apply_patch emit PreToolUse events, with the patch/diff text in tool_input.command -- the same field name Bash uses, not a separate content/new_string field like Claude Code's Write/Edit.

hooks._command_comment: Same script as the Bash matcher above -- it reads tool_input.command regardless of tool_name, so one script covers both matchers.
hooks.statusMessage: Wingman: scanning file edit for secret patterns

hooks._PostToolUse_comment: Added in a follow-up 2026-07-25 pass, same research session as the hooks above. A direct fetch of learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks confirmed PostToolUse's payload field for a tool's output is `tool_response` -- the same field name Claude Code uses, so secret-scanner.mjs/content-injection-scanner.mjs/session-health.mjs/context-monitor.mjs all port over with no field-name translation for that half. No matcher is set below (fires on every tool call), matching each canonical hook's own 'all tools' registration. Still schema-confirmed only, not live-tested -- same discipline as the PreToolUse hooks above.

hooks._command_comment: Ported from plugins/wingman/hooks/secret-scanner.mjs -- warn-only (never blocks): flags a secret that surfaced in a tool's OUTPUT (e.g. an echoed token), complementing secret-guard.mjs's input-side block above.
hooks.statusMessage: Wingman: scanning tool output for secret patterns

hooks._command_comment: Ported from plugins/wingman/hooks/content-injection-scanner.mjs -- warn-only: flags prompt-injection phrasing surfacing in fetched/read content (a web page, a file, a PR comment), not just the founder's own prompt (see prompt-guard below).
hooks.statusMessage: Wingman: scanning tool output for prompt-injection phrasing

hooks._command_comment: Ported from plugins/wingman/hooks/session-health.mjs -- tracks a per-project tool-call count, warns YELLOW at 40 and RED at 60, writes .wingman/session-health.json.

Ported from plugins/wingman/hooks/context-monitor.mjs -- estimates context-window usage from payload size and tracks scope creep (files edited outside the project root). The scope-creep half is a genuine ADAPTATION, not a direct port: it parses apply_patch's own V4A patch-header lines ('*** Update File: ...') out of tool_input.command to recover a file path, since Codex's apply_patch has no separate file_path field the way Claude Code's Edit/Write do -- see the script's own header comment for the full disclosure of what's confirmed vs. inferred here.
hooks.statusMessage: Wingman: monitoring context usage and scope

hooks._UserPromptSubmit_comment: Added in the same 2026-07-25 pass: UserPromptSubmit is CONFIRMED to exist (fires 'before model processes user input', per the docs) with the prompt text in a field literally named `prompt` -- the exact same field name Claude Code uses. This was a genuinely open question earlier passes of this adapter left unresolved ('no confirmed UserPromptSubmit analog'); it's real. No matcher is supported for this event (matcher values are documented as ignored if configured), matching the registration below.

hooks._command_comment: Ported from plugins/wingman/hooks/prompt-guard.mjs -- scans the founder's own prompt for classic injection phrasing (instruction override, role hijack, system-prompt reveal, exfiltration) before the model sees it.
hooks.statusMessage: Wingman: scanning prompt for injection phrasing

hooks._SessionStart_comment: Added in the same 2026-07-25 pass: SessionStart is CONFIRMED to exist, with matcher values startup/resume/clear/compact (a strict superset of Claude Code's own startup/resume/clear -- Codex additionally re-fires SessionStart after a compaction). No matcher set below, so it fires on all four, matching the canonical hook's own 'run on every session start' behavior.

hooks._command_comment: Ported from plugins/wingman/hooks/session-start.mjs -- initializes .wingman/state.json on first run and surfaces a summary of the previous session (tool-call count, warnings) via systemMessage.

hooks._PreCompact_comment: Added in the same 2026-07-25 pass: PreCompact is CONFIRMED to exist, matcher values manual/auto (same pair Claude Code uses). Genuine disclosed gap: PreCompact's documented input fields (trigger, turn_id, session_id) do NOT include cwd, unlike SessionStart/PreToolUse/PostToolUse -- the script below falls back to process.cwd() when cwd is absent from the payload, same defensive fallback the canonical hook already used.

hooks._command_comment: Ported from plugins/wingman/hooks/pre-compact-guard.mjs -- warn-only: reminds the agent to commit/checkpoint real uncommitted work before its reasoning gets compacted away.
hooks.statusMessage: Wingman: checking for uncommitted work before compaction

hooks._Stop_comment: Added in the same 2026-07-25 pass: Stop is CONFIRMED to exist (no matcher supported). TWO genuine, disclosed gaps versus Claude Code's own Stop: (1) documented input is turn_id/stop_hook_active/last_assistant_message -- no transcript_path, so the ported evaluate()'s stall-detection check (repeated identical tool calls) has no real data to run against here and is wired as a permanent no-op (always passed an empty array) until a real tool-call-history field is confirmed for this event; (2) no cwd field documented either -- the script falls back to process.cwd() unconditionally. The completion-promise and wall-clock-budget checks are unaffected by either gap and port over cleanly.

hooks._command_comment: Ported from plugins/wingman/hooks/stop-loop.mjs -- opt-in autonomous loop, disabled unless .wingman/loop.json sets enabled: true. See the script's own header for the disclosed stall-detection gap.
hooks.statusMessage: Wingman: checking whether the loop's completion promise has been met

hooks._dod_structural_gate_decision: DELIBERATELY NOT PORTED as a Codex-native hook, despite PreToolUse's Bash matcher + tool_input.command now being fully confirmed (same schema secret-guard.mjs above already uses). plugins/wingman/scripts/dod-pre-push-check.mjs already reuses dod-structural-gate.mjs's exact pure functions (checkBoardroomVerdictClean, checkVerdictTranscriptionMatchesDetails, checkTestPresence, detectTestCommand, runTestSuite, checkThreatRegisterCleanAcrossArtifacts) as a real git pre-push hook, which fires at the git level under ANY harness -- including this one -- with zero Codex-specific wiring, exactly the same way the PreToolUse Bash matcher above already recommends for this exact gate (see its own _command_comment). Building a second, Codex-hooks.json-specific PreToolUse wrapper around the same pure functions would be pure duplication with no behavioral gain: both paths fire on the same `git push` command, gate on the same checkpoint data, and the git-level path additionally works for a human typing `git push` directly, which a Codex-hooks.json entry never would. No new file was added for this.
